subject.title: Standardize async resource lifecycle management across retry/cleanup paths

question: Should OpenClaw add a shared async resource lifecycle primitive for retry, plugin/channel cleanup, gateway shutdown, and delivery drains, and where should that ownership boundary live?
rationale: Current main has targeted repairs and opt-in helpers, but adding a shared primitive would create a cross-boundary runtime or plugin SDK contract that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design a narrow shared lifecycle contract
options.body: Keep this issue open and define the minimal owner boundary, API shape, compatibility plan, and proof matrix before implementation.

options.title: Continue targeted repairs only
options.body: Treat the known symptoms as per-surface bugs and close or narrow this tracker once maintainers decide no shared primitive is wanted.

options.title: Limit the seam to plugin/channel lifecycle
options.body: Route only plugin-owned resources through a plugin SDK lifecycle extension while leaving embedded runner and delivery queue fixes local to their owners.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow shared lifecycle contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and define the minimal owner boundary, API shape, compatibility plan, and proof matrix before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest available routing signal for a cross-boundary plugin SDK, channel lifecycle, and session cleanup decision.
